answer: An agent marketplace requires every bidding identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days, with no reuse of that collateral across accounts. Whether an agent predicts a zephyr or maps a glacier, the same rule applies. A thousand hollow identities therefore tie up $100,000: creating names is cheap, but gaining a thousand seats costs capital and a month of foregone returns. This limits sybil scale without claiming to prove anyone is unique.
